reading.text:
Unit: def:LevyStochCalc.Brownian.sigmaBrownian (reading locked before any Lean is seen)

Paper notion. Section 2 (lines 224-229): W is a d-dimensional BM "and an independent Poisson random
measure N", with "an independent initial sigma-field F_0"; the filtration is generated by W, N and F_0.
The sigma-field generated by the Brownian motion is sigma(W) = sigma(W_s : s >= 0) (all times, all
components), used to express the independence of W from N and F_0; a time-indexed variant
sigma(W_s : s <= t) is the Brownian part of the generated filtration.

What a faithful Lean definition must be.
- The sigma-algebra on Omega generated by the BM: supremum over s (in the time index, possibly s <= t if
  time-indexed) and over components j of comap W^j_s (Borel). For independence purposes it must be the
  whole-path sigma-algebra (all s >= 0, or at least all s <= T), not one time.
- Raw (no null sets); <= ambient when each W_s is measurable.
- If it is time-indexed, it should be monotone in t and equal the natural filtration of W (unit 07).

comparison.text:
Comparison: def:LevyStochCalc.Brownian.sigmaBrownian
(Brownian/MultidimFiltered.lean:32-34; used in LevyDriver.indep as sup_i sigmaBrownian (W.W i).)

- Reading: sigma(W) = sup over times (and components) of comap W_s, whole-path, raw, <= ambient.
- Lean: for a 1-dim BrownianMotion, sup over t : R of comap (W.W t) Borel - the sigma-algebra generated
  by all values, whole path, raw. The d-dimensional sigma(W) is sup_i sigmaBrownian (W.W i), as used in
  LevyDriver.indep. Values at t < 0 are a.s. 0 and contribute only P-trivial events.

Verdict: faithful with representation choices (R-indexed time; negative-time values P-trivial;
per-component, the vector version being the supremum over components at the use site).

verdict.detail:
Representation choices, each harmless:
1. Defined for a single real BrownianMotion; the sigma-algebra of the d-dimensional W is the supremum over
   components (as LevyDriver.indep writes it), which equals sigma(W_s, s >= 0) for the vector process.
2. The supremum runs over all t : R; for t < 0, W_t = 0 a.s., so these add only events of probability 0 or
   1, which do not affect any independence statement.
